clue.text: Old civilisation that created centaurs?

parts.note: points to the ancient people of central Italy whose painted pottery and bronzes are full of mythical horse-men

explanation.definitionFit: The people of ancient Etruria, before Rome rose, were an old civilisation whose art often shows centaurs.

clue.text: Form basis of lower position, of course

parts.note: on a golf course the position of the ball is its lie

explanation.surface: A golfer reflects that a ball's low position is the basis of the hole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' is a golf course, where the lie is where the ball rests.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that lies beneath another thing forms its foundation, so it supports or forms the basis of it.

clue.text: Spooner performing for nosy parker

indicators.note: performing suggests the letters of the name are put through their paces into a new order

explanation.surface: The famous Oxford don, playing a part, takes the role of a busybody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spooner' tempts you to swap initial sounds, but here the name is just anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosy parker is a busybody who pries into others' business, a prying person.

clue.text: It takes a good man to chop tree in way of traffic

parts.note: a good man is a saint, abbreviated ST

indicators.note: to chop the tree is to break its letters up and rearrange them

explanation.surface: Only a good person would fell a tree that stands in the path of the cars.
explanation.definitionFit: A road in a town carries vehicles, so it is a way of traffic.

clue.text: Thin fabric of suits tailored by English

indicators.note: tailored means cut and made up anew, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: An English tailor makes fine garments from a delicate material.
explanation.definitionFit: Tissue is a light, gauzy woven cloth, a fine and delicate material.

clue.text: Strange Atlantic noise former scourge of sailors

indicators.note: strange suggests the letters are made odd, set into an unfamiliar order

explanation.surface: An eerie sound out on the ocean once terrified seamen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scourge' is a whip here, not a plague.
explanation.definitionFit: The nine-thonged whip was the naval punishment once used to flog seamen, literally a lash.

clue.text: Ticker-tape technician?

parts.note: the ticker is the heart, and the tape is the paper trace a heart-monitoring machine prints

explanation.definitionFit: A technician who records the heart's electrical activity on a paper strip works with the heart, slang the ticker.

clue.text: Get away from here!

parts.note: read not as a rude dismissal but as an instruction: this is the place where a race or journey sets off

explanation.definitionFit: A race begins at the spot where competitors set off, so its origin is where you get away.

clue.text: Small Greek and. English river-bird

parts.note: small signals the short form: GR abbreviates Greek
the Ouse is a river in England, flowing through York

explanation.surface: A little Greek and an Englishman watch a waterfowl.
explanation.walkthrough: The OUSE is a river in Yorkshire, and another in East Anglia.
explanation.definitionFit: The red grouse is a game bird of the moors.

clue.text: So, a variation includes a stanza abroad

indicators.note: includes means the anagram wraps around the next piece
a variation on the two short words means their letters are reordered

parts.note: a stanza is a verse of a poem

explanation.surface: A poet revises a piece and adds a stanza while travelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variation' turns SO A into OAS, which 'includes' VERSE: O + VERSE + AS.
explanation.definitionFit: Being abroad means being in a foreign country, across the sea.

clue.text: Knock back average amount

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for average from right to left

parts.note: par is the average or normal amount

explanation.surface: Someone is criticising a mediocre quantity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock' looks like a verb meaning criticise with 'back', but it is the definition, a tap on a door.
explanation.definitionFit: A rap is a sharp tap, as on a door.

clue.text: Calif's overthrowing the public treasury

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective, meaning relating to the public treasury

indicators.note: overthrowing suggests the ruler's word is toppled and its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: A caliph is toppled and the state coffers are seized.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-S of "Calif's" supplies a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiscal matters concern government revenue, the state's funds and taxation.

clue.text: Plea made in civic centre at Yeovil

indicators.note: made in says the answer is produced inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: An appeal is delivered at the town hall of a Somerset town.
explanation.walkthrough: Yeovil is a market town in Somerset, England.
explanation.definitionFit: An entreaty is an earnest request or appeal.

clue.text: Perhaps a single track

explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a single is one run scored; and a run is a track, as a ski slope or animal trail.

clue.text: Great sufferings of the endlessly sea-going sort

indicators.note: sort as a verb means arrange, so the remaining letters are put in a new order
endlessly means the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Seafarers are the type who endure great hardship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the last G of SEAGOING to leave SEAGOIN, which 'sort' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Agonies are extreme pains or torments, great distress.

clue.text: Union promise speaking with false tongue

explanation.definitionFit: At a wedding each partner vows assent with these two words; and Ido is an invented international language, an artificial speech.

clue.text: Hanging makes one gasp for breath about the finish

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: to gasp for breath is to pant

explanation.surface: A runner pants for air as the finish line comes into view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hanging' sounds like an execution, but it is the adjective suspended.
explanation.definitionFit: Pendant as an adjective means dangling or suspended from above.

clue.text: The writing on the wall

parts.note: not the idiom for a sign of doom but literally lettering carved on a building or monument

explanation.definitionFit: An epigraph is an inscription, words engraved on stone or a building.

clue.text: Making bone casts for fun?

parts.note: dice were once made of bone and are called bones; casts are throws of them

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bone casts' suggests plaster for a fracture; it means throws of dice, which are slang 'bones'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaming with cubes means throwing them, and dice are nicknamed bones.

clue.text: Wayward lad hiding in oak, for example, needs the pressure of a foot

definitions.text: needs the pressure of a foot
definitions.note: describes the device by what operates it: a lever worked by pushing with the foot

indicators.note: hiding in means sitting concealed inside the other piece

parts.note: an oak is an example of a tree

indicators.note: wayward means wandering off course, so the letters stray into a new order

explanation.surface: A naughty boy hides in an oak tree and must be kicked out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wayward' makes ADL from LAD, and 'hiding in' puts it inside TREE.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadle is a pedal lever that drives a machine, such as an old sewing machine, when pushed down by the foot.

clue.text: Assume control of deliveries?

parts.note: to take charge is the phrase, but deliveries hints at cricket, where six balls bowled make one over

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled, called deliveries.
explanation.definitionFit: To take charge is the meaning; a business buyout is the noun form, and cricket's six deliveries form an over.

clue.text: Start exciting to anger, in way way

definitions.text: Start exciting to anger, in way way

indicators.note: start points to the opening letter of the next word
as printed this reads as a garbled 'in a way', a phrase saying the letters are arranged in some fashion

explanation.surface: A provocateur finds a fresh method to begin stirring up rage.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer: to excite to anger. The printed 'in way way' stands for an anagram signal such as 'in a way'.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrage is to provoke someone into fury, rousing their temper.

clue.text: Evensong from St Genevieve's, perhaps

indicators.note: from says the answer is taken out of the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: A service of evening prayer is held at the church of St Genevieve.
explanation.definitionFit: Vespers is the evening service of prayer in church, so the singular names that sung evening office.

clue.text: Absorb food into body by breaking up pectin

indicators.note: breaking up means the word is split apart and its letters reassembled

explanation.surface: Digestion breaks down the gelling agent in jam.
explanation.walkthrough: Pectin is the gelling substance in fruit, used in jam.
explanation.definitionFit: Incept is a biological term for ingesting, taking nourishment in.

clue.text: Work unit of power generators

indicators.note: of indicates the answer is a part taken out of the following words

explanation.surface: An electrical engineer measures the output of power stations.
explanation.definitionFit: The erg is the CGS unit of energy, one dyne acting over one centimetre.

clue.text: Who is in possession of this power to influence? Daily is, to a degree

parts.note: a daily is a cleaner who comes in each day, also called a char
MA, Master of Arts, is a degree

explanation.surface: Asking who owns this persuasive gift, a newspaper suggests it is somewhat present.
explanation.walkthrough: A CHAR or daily is an old British term for a cleaning lady. 'to a degree' looks like 'somewhat'; MA is the degree.
explanation.definitionFit: Charisma is compelling charm that inspires devotion, a personal magnetism.

clue.text: To refresh, go to resort

explanation.definitionFit: To mend or restore something is one sense; to betake oneself to a place, as to repair to the bar, is the other.

clue.text: Huge plane tore apart jumbo out of control

indicators.note: tore apart means the letters are ripped up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A giant aircraft breaks up as an airliner spins out of control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumbo' suggests a jet with the plane, but it is the elephant.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild bull elephant separated from its herd is dangerous; jumbo is a nickname for an elephant.
